description: Golden groundedness dataset. Frozen mini-corpus + questions with known support. Release gates: fabricated_citations == 0, claim_support_rate >= 0.98 on supported questions, refusal_correctness >= 0.95 on unsupported questions.

corpus.title: RAG and hallucination study
corpus.text: Retrieval-augmented generation reduces hallucination rates by grounding outputs in retrieved passages. In our controlled study across three domains, RAG reduced factual errors by 37% compared to closed-book generation. However, retrieval failures propagate: when the retriever returned irrelevant passages, error rates exceeded the closed-book baseline by 12%.

corpus.title: Free-tier model evaluation
corpus.text: Smaller instruction-tuned models follow extraction schemas reliably when outputs are constrained to JSON and validated programmatically. In our benchmark, schema-validated extraction recovered 94% of target fields, compared to 71% for unconstrained prose extraction with the same model.

corpus.title: Cross-encoder limitations
corpus.text: Cross-encoder relevance scores correlate poorly with entailment judgments. Sentence pairs with opposite polarity, such as negated statements, received near-identical relevance scores in 83% of tested cases, confirming that similarity-based scoring cannot substitute for natural language inference.

corpus.title: Hybrid retrieval fusion
corpus.text: Combining dense embedding retrieval with lexical BM25 through reciprocal rank fusion improved recall@10 by 18% over dense-only retrieval on our benchmark. The two methods surface complementary results: dense retrieval captures paraphrase, while BM25 anchors rare exact terms such as identifiers and numbers.

corpus.title: Chunk size and grounding
corpus.text: Smaller retrieval chunks improved citation precision but reduced context sufficiency. At 256 tokens, 88% of cited spans exactly located the supporting sentence, versus 64% at 1024 tokens, but answers at 256 tokens more often omitted necessary surrounding context, raising the refusal rate by 9 points.

corpus.title: Refusal calibration
corpus.text: When the corpus lacked supporting evidence, an explicit refusal was rated more trustworthy than a confident unsupported answer by a margin of 31 percentage points in a user study of 240 participants. Labeling the gap, rather than hedging, drove most of the trust gain.

corpus.title: Quote-match verification
corpus.text: Requiring a verbatim quote per generated claim, checked by normalized exact matching against the cited chunk, drove fabricated citations to zero across 1,000 generated claims. Because an exact quote cannot be satisfied by a paraphrase, the constraint holds even for small, weak models.
